name: Total

summary.text: Total is the French oil and gas company now trading as TotalEnergies. A 2021 peer-reviewed study by Christophe Bonneuil, Pierre-Louis Choquet and Benjamin Franta in Global Environmental Change found, from archival research and interviews with former executives, that Total's staff were alerted as early as 1971, through an article in the company magazine Total Information, to the risk of severe warming from fossil fuels, that the company cast doubt on the science in the late 1980s, and that from the late 1990s it accepted the science while favouring delayed policy responses. On October 23, 2025 the Paris Judicial Court ruled, in a case brought by Greenpeace France, Friends of the Earth France and Notre Affaire à Tous under French consumer law, that TotalEnergies' claims about aiming for carbon neutrality by 2050 and being a major player in the energy transition were misleading commercial practices.

facts.claim: The study 'Early warnings and emerging accountability: Total's responses to global warming, 1971-2021' by Bonneuil, Choquet and Franta was published in Global Environmental Change (volume 71, article 102386) on October 19, 2021, drawing on archival research and interviews with former executives.

sources.title: Early warnings and emerging accountability: Total's responses to global warming, 1971-2021
Early warnings and emerging accountability: Total's responses to global warming

facts.claim: The study's central finding is that Total's personnel were alerted to the risk of severe warming from its products as early as 1971, that the company became better informed during the 1980s, began casting doubt on the science in the late 1980s, and by the late 1990s had shifted to accepting climate science while favouring delayed or peripheral policy responses.

sources.title: Alertes précoces et émergence d'une responsabilité environnementale

facts.claim: The 1971 warning identified by the study appeared in Total Information, a company magazine with a circulation of about 6,000 read by employees, executives and commercial partners, which discussed rising atmospheric CO2 from fossil-fuel burning.

sources.title: Total knew about climate change in 1971, study finds
Total conocía las consecuencias del cambio climático y promovió dudas

facts.claim: On October 23, 2025 the Paris Judicial Court ruled that TotalEnergies had engaged in misleading commercial practices: its claims about aiming for carbon neutrality by 2050 and being a major player in the energy transition were likely to mislead consumers while the company increased oil and gas production. The court dismissed the part of the case concerning the marketing of fossil gas and biofuels.

sources.title: French court convicts TotalEnergies over misleading climate claims
French Court Rules TotalEnergies Misled Consumers with Climate Claims
TotalEnergies fined for greenwashing in its advertising in French ruling

facts.claim: The case was brought by Greenpeace France, Friends of the Earth France and Notre Affaire à Tous under French consumer law; the court awarded 8,000 euros in damages to each of the three organisations plus 15,000 euros in legal costs, and ordered the company to remove or revise the claims and publish the decision, with daily penalties for non-compliance.

sources.title: French court convicts TotalEnergies over misleading climate claims
TotalEnergies ordered to revise climate messaging after landmark Paris Court ruling

facts.claim: ClientEarth described the October 2025 ruling as the first conviction of an oil company for corporate greenwashing, and it was reported as the first application of France's consumer-law provisions on misleading environmental claims to a fossil-fuel company; TotalEnergies disputed the greenwashing characterisation after the ruling.

openQuestions: The site's 'total' entity conflates the oil company with unrelated uses of the word on the Crash Conduits page ('Total Information Awareness', 'total return swap'); the extractor should treat 'Total' as an alias of 'totalenergies' or restrict it to the Carbon Ledger page.

Site claim that Total's 1971 magazine article was by climatologist François Durand-Dastès and projected about 400 ppm by 2010 was not confirmed in the sources opened, which describe the article without naming the author or the projection; the paper's full text should settle it.
Site claim that 'by the late 1980s Total was promoting doubt' is supported by the study's abstract.

Sources differ on the remedies in the October 2025 ruling (withdrawal within a month under a 10,000-euro daily penalty, versus publishing a link to the decision for 180 days under a 20,000-euro daily penalty); the judgment text should be checked. Whether TotalEnergies has appealed was not established.
No source opened documents the 2021 renaming of Total to TotalEnergies, so no connection between the 'total' and 'totalenergies' ids was recorded.
